title: A Study Assessing Eloralintide (LY3841136) in Healthy Participants
official: A Phase 1 Open-Label Study to Determine the Effect of Injection Site on the Relative Bioavailability of a Single Subcutaneous Dose of LY3841136 and to Evaluate the Pharmacokinetics of a Single Intravenous Dose of LY3841136 in Healthy Participants
summary: The main purpose of this study is to investigate the effects of where Eloralintide is subcutaneously (SC) injected into the body and to investigate how the body processes an intravenous (IV) dose of Eloralintide. Blood tests will be performed to investigate how the study drug affects the body. For each participant, the study will last about 12 weeks and will include a stay in the Clinical Research Unit (CRU) lasting 6 nights.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Are overtly healthy as determined by medical evaluation
* Are 18 to 65 years of age inclusive, at the time of signing the informed consent.
* Have a body mass index (BMI) within the range of 23.0 to 40.0 kilograms per square meter (kg/m²), inclusive.
* Have had self-reported stable weight for the 3 months prior to screening, that is, less than 5 percent (%) body weight change.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Have known allergies to related compounds of eloralintide, or any of the components of the formulations.
* Have been diagnosed with Type 1 or Type 2 diabetes mellitus.
* Have a history of any malignancy within the past 5 years except for basal cell or squamous epithelial carcinomas of the skin that have been resected with no evidence of metastatic disease for 3 years.
* Have a history or presence of a gastrointestinal disorder or previous surgery that impacts gastric emptying.
* Have obesity induced by other endocrinologic disorders, or diagnosed monogenetic or syndromic forms of obesity.
* Have a history or presence of psychiatric disorders.
* Have a history of chronic medical conditions involving the heart, liver, or kidneys.
* Have a history of hypocalcemia or hypercalcemia.
* Have a medical history or current evidence of clinically significant cardiac condition.
